summary.text: Beth Grimshaw is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Croydon at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in disability support, is a mother of three and has rented in Melbourne's outer east all her life. She says she has campaigned for safer pedestrian crossings in the Yarra Valley and taken part in local conservation work, anti-racism campaigns and anti-war protests.

priorities.text: to fight for the better world that we all deserve
Affordable mental health and preventive care
Fairer taxes to pay for action on living costs and housing
A faster shift to renewable energy

sources.title: Croydon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Beth Grimshaw, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: David Vanderwolf is running as a community independent in Croydon at the 2026 Victorian election, with the endorsement of the Voices of Deakin group. An economist by profession, he works in the state Treasury and Finance department, having earlier held public service jobs in the ACT and in Victoria's environment department. Before entering the public service he held jobs in flooring, children's party entertainment and online retail, and he lives in Croydon South.

occupation.text: Economist, Victorian Department of Treasury and Finance

priorities.text: My party room is the people of Croydon
Planning reform so new housing suits local needs and is affordable
Lower grocery prices and less food waste
Tighter rules on political donations and a law against misleading election advertising
Refusing donations from vested interest groups

summary.text: Glenn Brindley is One Nation's candidate for Croydon at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC, his career has been in logistics and business development management for businesses in the compressed air and vacuum sector, and he has served as president of a club in the Eastern Football League. One Nation's candidate page refused automated requests, so it could not be checked.

occupation.text: Logistics manager and business development manager

prior_roles.note: The ABC doesn't name the club, give years or say whether he still holds the post.

sources.title: Croydon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Lini Fernando is the Greens candidate for Croydon at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a lawyer whose practice has covered human rights, anti-corruption and environmental matters. On the party's site she describes herself as a migrant, a woman of colour and a mother raising a young family in the area.

priorities.text: I firmly believe that social justice and environmental justice go hand in hand
More affordable housing and relief from living costs
Well-funded public services
Stronger action on climate change

sources.title: Croydon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Lini Fernando, Candidate for Croydon, Australian Greens

summary.text: Nathan Schwab is the Libertarian candidate for Croydon at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he grew up in Mooroolbark, went to Mooroolbark College and still lives in the area, and that he studied civil engineering at Deakin University and is now a design engineer. He says Victoria's handling of the pandemic deepened his worries about government overreach.

priorities.text: Lower taxes and less red tape for people and businesses
Careful, responsible use of public money
Courts and policing that protect the community and make offenders answer for their crimes
Firm limits on government power and more transparency

summary.text: Nofoao Thomas is the Family First candidate for Croydon at the 2026 Victorian election, according to the VEC's list of nominations. Before nominations closed, the ABC guide and the party's list of Victorian candidates had him standing in Evelyn. Neither had published a biography of him as at early November 2026.

summary.text: Richard Farr is standing for Labor in Croydon at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in the area and has spent most of his life there, with over ten years of work in the retail and hospitality trades. He is a committee member of the Melbourne Highland Games and Celtic Festival, an event held within the district.

prior_roles.organisation: Melbourne Highland Games and Celtic Festival

priorities.text: Keeping working from home available to employees
Better public transport for the Croydon area
Fixing local roads so travel times come down

sources.title: Croydon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Richard Farr, Candidate for Croydon, Victorian Labor

summary.text: Toby Wooldridge became the Liberal candidate for Croydon in October 2026, endorsed by the party's state executive at the meeting that dropped its first choice, Grant Hutchinson. He is a demographer and an associate director at a geographic data company, and has worked in property economics as an analyst and consultant since 2017. The ABC notes that his father is former federal health minister Michael Wooldridge and his aunt is former state minister Mary Wooldridge.

occupation.text: Demographer; associate director at a geographic data firm

priorities.text: More police and tougher laws to improve safety in Croydon
Fixing potholes and upgrading local roads
Abolishing Labor taxes to ease the cost of living
Better health services at Maroondah Hospital
Planning for the future of local schools

sources.title: Croydon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Toby Wooldridge, Liberal for Croydon, Liberal Victoria
